slides.alt_text: Editorial slide: A preview of the Last Supper? Melchizedek brings out bread and wine. Jesus later shares bread and wine at the Last Supper. Christians have connected the two meals for centuries.

slides.alt_text: Editorial slide: Why Christians connect them Hebrews already compares Melchizedek’s priesthood with Jesus. That made his bread and wine a natural symbol of Communion for early Christians.
slides.body: Hebrews already compares Melchizedek’s priesthood with Jesus. That made his bread and wine a natural symbol of Communion for early Christians.

slides.alt_text: Editorial slide: But Genesis describes a meal Genesis does not call the bread and wine a sacrifice or say they predict a future meal. Hebrews discusses Melchizedek at length but never mentions them. The link arose later.
